column1: # docs/map.tsv: the place in the org chart of every tracked path.
# Read it like CODEOWNERS: gitignore-style patterns, and the last row that matches a path
# wins. A pattern with a slash in it is anchored at the repo root, `*` stays inside one
# directory, `**` crosses directories, and a pattern that names a directory covers
# everything under it. `python3 bin/check-docs.py map` (bin/check.sh §22) reports a tracked
# path that only the catch-all row matches, a page that does not exist, and a directorate
# or division the chart does not have. `python3 bin/check-docs.py map --list` prints every
# Two kinds of row, tab-separated, "-" for an empty column:
#   =<directorate>[/<division>]  title  page                 the chart, in reading order
#   pattern  directorate  division  branch  page             a rule
# The page is the one that documents the path: a division page, or a module's README.
# bin/gen-org-doc.py draws the chart in README.md and docs/README.md from the chart rows.
# --- the catch-all: a path that only this row matches is unmapped ----------------------
# Arch Linux: the user layer, the installer, roles and lists, the system layer, snapshots, hosts
# Windows: the renderer, the units, dram.ps1, debloat, the boot guard, install media
# Themes: the palettes, their generators, the switcher, day and night, wallpaper, app themes
# Shell & bars: Hyprland, the bars, launchers and notifications, the terminal, boot screens
# the desktop role: the standard app set, on the Toolchain page
# Development: the dev kit, containers, the editor, ML, sysadmin
# Packaging: the [dram] repo, Flatpak, the winget lists
# Profiles: office, college, re-lab, creator, gaming, emulation, chat
# Boot trust: Secure Boot, UKIs, TPM2, Windows' own ESP
# Network: the firewall and host hardening, DNS, NetworkManager
# Software supply: the register, integrity checks, pins
# Quality: the repo checks, the tests, CI
